A_target.statement:
Let $p$ be a [[Definition:Probability Distribution|probability distribution]] on a set of $n$ points.
Then:
:$\map H p \le \log n$
with equality {{iff}} $p$ is [[Definition:Discrete Uniform Distribution|uniform]].

B_source.statement:
Let $p, q$ be [[Definition:Probability Distribution|probability distributions]] on a finite set.
Then:
:$\map D {p \parallel q} = \displaystyle \sum_i p_i \log \frac {p_i} {q_i} \ge 0$
with equality {{iff}} $p = q$.

substitutions.the reference distribution q: the uniform distribution on the finite set
substitutions.the relative entropy between p and q: the gap between the logarithm of n and the entropy of p
substitutions.the equality case of the inequality: the case where p is uniform

derived.nonnegativity of relative entropy: the entropy of p is at most the logarithm of n
derived.the equality condition: the maximum is attained exactly at the uniform distribution

validity_conditions: Taking the reference distribution to be uniform makes the relative entropy equal the logarithm of n minus the entropy of p, by direct expansion.
Nonnegativity of relative entropy then gives the bound, and its equality condition gives uniqueness of the maximizer.
The set must be finite for the uniform distribution to exist; on a countably infinite set there is no uniform distribution and entropy is unbounded.
proof_plan:
Hence:
:$\map D {p \parallel q} = \log n - \map H p$
